name: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma, lymphocyte-rich type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: World Health Organization (WHO) Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of classic Reed-Sternberg cells or variants in a background rich in small lymphocytes
Immunohistochemistry showing CD30 positivity and CD15 negativity or weak positivity, with strong CD20 and PAX5 expression in background lymphocytes
Histological pattern demonstrating a predominance of small lymphocytes with sparse eosinophils and plasma cells
Exclusion of nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma by morphology and immunophenotype

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of Reed-Sternberg cells in a lymphocyte-rich background with characteristic immunophenotype (CD30 positive, CD15 negative or weak) and exclusion of other lymphoma subtypes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histopathology, immunophenotyping, and clinical correlation.

searchTerms: neck lymph node swelling without pain

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of Reed-Sternberg cells on lymph node biopsy
searchTerms: presence of specific abnormal cells in lymph node biopsy
Reed-Sternberg cells found in lymph tissue
diagnostic cells seen in lymph node sample

common.symptomName: B symptoms (fever >38°C, night sweats, weight loss >10%)
common.notes: May be absent in lymphocyte-rich subtype
searchTerms: fever, night sweats, and weight loss
classic systemic symptoms including fever and sweating
B symptoms like fever and weight loss

common.notes: Secondary to marrow involvement or chronic disease

lymph node pain triggered by alcohol
pain in lymph nodes after drinking alcohol

occasional.symptomName: Cough due to mediastinal mass effect
searchTerms: persistent cough due to chest tumor
nerve problems due to CNS disease
itching with high eosinophil counts linked to cancer
cancer-related pruritus with immune cell increase

imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing mediastinal lymphadenopathy
genetic: No specific recurrent genetic mutations; clonal rearrangement of immunoglobulin genes in background lymphocytes
other: Histopathology showing classic Reed-Sternberg cells in a lymphocyte-rich background
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD30 and PAX5, negative or weak CD15

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of 'popcorn' or L&H cells instead of classic Reed-Sternberg cells
Strong CD20 positivity and CD30 negativity
Fibrous bands dividing lymph node into nodules
Different immunophenotypic markers (e.g., CD20 positivity without CD30)

redFlags: Unexplained persistent fever and night sweats
Signs of airway obstruction or superior vena cava syndrome
